correctness.rationale: For any shore/color combination all corresponding labelled vertices have the same deterministic next color; the full state map therefore factors through exactly 15^3 nonempty support triples with tagged original color representatives. The supplied runnable finite certificate exhausts all 3375 triples, verifies F^10=F^6 at every initial tagged representative, finds exact first-4-period entry depths (620,248,658,739,641,391,78), excludes period two and nonzero fixed points in the 620 recurrent triples, proves the 619 shared primitive-four support classes and their identical next-step transitions under Greenberg-Hastings and cyclic-contact maps, and enumerates 1442 extinction-support triples. The two explicit symmetric support-cardinality coefficient tables are recomputed and checked, then lifted by inclusion-exclusion surjection counts. A direct vertex-wise enumeration of 353600 labelled configurations across eight graph sizes agrees with all formulas, but does not by itself establish the all-size theorem. Witnesses on K111 and K112 show sharp depths five and six. In the extinction table the unique maximal balanced exponential monomial is 4 U3(n)^3, so the claimed probability 4(27/64)^n(1+O((2/3)^n)) is correct.

The exact 13-term extinction-basin enumeration answers a natural uncomputed size-dependent invariant for an infinite family; balanced extinction has a sharp rare-event exponent 27/64 and an explicit four-support dominant mechanism. These have direct significance for the stability and basins of excitable waves. The dependence on a finite exhaustive certificate is openly stated, as is the pre-existing numeric four-cycle census.
